extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, presidential and congressional policymakers, and courts involved in agency rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and standards for improving the effectiveness and efficiency of federal legislative (notice-and-comment) rulemaking, directed to the President, Congress, courts, and agency management. Covers presidential review, congressional structuring, judicial review, APA amendments, and agency internal management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential oversight reserved for most important rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Presidential oversight and review should be reserved for the most important rules, and agencies should be given clear policy guidance in a directive, approved by the President, specifying what is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oversight should avoid extensive delays and be open to public scrutiny. The President’s policy should encourage planning and coordination, early dialogue between agencies and the reviewing entity, and preservation of a unified agenda. Additional non-APA analytical requirements should be kept to a minimum and periodically reassessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential directive content and implementation principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The President’s program for coordination and review of agency rules should be set forth in a directive that is reviewed periodically, sensitive to burdens on rulemaking, and implemented so it does not unduly delay or constrain rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The directive and the oversight entity’s procedures should (1) promote early dialogue and coordination in identifying rules for review; (2) set forth relevant analytical requirements and provide interpretive guidance; (3) ensure expedition and openness in the process; (4) support planning and tracking of regulatory initiatives; and (5) encourage consensual processes such as negotiated rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congress should refrain from program-specific procedural mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress generally should refrain from imposing program-specific rulemaking procedures or analytical requirements beyond those required by the APA (5 U.S.C. § 553).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When additional procedures are justified, they should be narrowly focused on identified problems and adopted incrementally or after experimentation. Statutes imposing on-the-record or hybrid adjudicative procedures in rulemaking should be repealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional time limits and use of 'regulatory hammers'
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress should not generally legislate time limits on rulemaking; if deadlines are imposed, Congress should ensure agencies have sufficient resources and should avoid statutory 'hammers' that automatically make policies effective upon deadline expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer judicial enforcement of prompt action (section 706(1)) to statutory automatic triggers. If a default rule is necessary, Congress should specify terms and avoid counterproductive automatic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrow statutory analytical requirements (focus on significant rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress should reconsider broadly applicable statutory analytical requirements (e.g., Regulatory Flexibility Act) and, if retained, focus them more narrowly on significant rules or particular categories of rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad requirements that apply to virtually all rules may be too burdensome and ineffective; confine special analyses to rules likely to be affected by the stated concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and timing of pre-enforcement judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-enforcement challenges should generally be permitted where the administrative record provides a sufficient basis for the court to resolve the issues; facial challenges and procedural challenges to the rulemaking should normally be allowed, while speculative challenges about possible applications should be deferred until application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows Abbott Laboratories standard: evaluate both fitness of issues and hardship of withholding review. Overuse of pre-enforcement review can induce precautionary challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional guidance for time-limited pre-enforcement review
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Congress mandates time limits for pre-enforcement review, it should generally specify that such review be requested within 90 days of issuance of the rule, provide direct review in courts of appeals, and limit stays to cases showing likelihood of success and significant private harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-limited review should be used only in specified situations (Recommendation 82-7) and should not preclude later enforcement-stage review except as Congress narrowly specifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'arbitrary and capricious' standard for review of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress should conform statutes to use the APA section 706(2)(A) 'arbitrary and capricious' standard for review of agency rules rather than the 'substantial evidence' test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The substantial evidence test has introduced confusion; the arbitrary-and-capricious test provides sufficient review in the informal rulemaking context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonize Chevron deference and 'hard look' review
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts should harmonize deferential Chevron review of statutory interpretation with the 'hard look' doctrine applied to an agency’s factual and policy justifications by emphasizing a two-step approach: determine limits of statutory authority and permissible factors, then defer to the agency’s reasonable selection among permissible choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulating this two-step approach more clearly would make review more consistent and predictable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts should avoid requiring greater justification than necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing agency rules, a reasoned statement that explains the basis and purpose of the rule and addresses significant issues raised in public comments should generally be adequate; courts should be sensitive not to require extra-APA procedures or excessive justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remands for failure to respond adequately to comments or to explain bases should be avoided when agency provides a reasoned response. Overly intrusive review increases defensive agency behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial specification of remedies and retroactivity considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing courts should, where feasible, specify which portions of a rule are set aside, vacated, stayed, or otherwise affected; consider whether unaffected portions should remain in effect; and weigh retroactivity and effects on parties not before the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts should ensure portions unaffected by illegality remain in effect unless inseverable, consider retroactivity of mandates, and recognize interests of persons not before the court in being heard or represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify minimum comment period (amend APA section 553)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend section 553(c) to specify that a comment period of 'no fewer than at least 30 days' be provided (with a good cause exception for shorter periods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 30-day period is a minimum, not a maximum; agencies are encouraged to allow longer comment periods and may leave record open for late comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codify 'logical outgrowth' doctrine for second-round notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 553 should specify that a second round of notice and comment is not required where the final rule is the 'logical outgrowth' of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This codifies generally accepted doctrine (e.g., South Terminal Corp. v. EPA) to avoid unnecessary second notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require a public rulemaking file and its contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 553 should require maintenance of a public rulemaking file beginning no later than the date an agency publishes an ANPRM or NPRM; agencies should make the file available to avoid reliance on FOIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rulemaking file should contain notices, written comments, and copies or an index of written factual material, studies, or reports substantially relied on or seriously considered (except as prohibited by law). Computerized access is encouraged government-wide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require a 'reasoned statement' responsive to significant comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the statement of basis and purpose requirement in section 553(c) to require a 'reasoned statement' (deleting 'conciseness') that includes a response to significant issues raised in public comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This codifies case law (e.g., State Farm) and discourages insubstantial arguments on review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate proprietary exemption and narrow military/foreign affairs exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate section 553(a)(2) exemption for rules relating to public property, loans, grants, benefits, or contracts; narrow section 553(a)(1) exemption for military and foreign affairs so that non-secret aspects are open to public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proprietary exemption is anachronistic; a modified exemption may remain for matters required by executive order to be secret in the interest of national defense or foreign policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set priorities and track rulemaking at senior agency levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior agency staff should develop management strategies to set priorities and track agency rulemaking initiatives, identifying who has authority to ensure schedules and policies are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic priority-setting and tracking helps ensure rulemaking proceeds efficiently and in line with agency policy goals (see Recommendation 87-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve presidential oversight entity early and establish internal review procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should seek to involve the presidential oversight entity early to reach agreement on the significance of rules, provide coordination, and speed final oversight review; establish internal review procedures at high levels to ensure compliance with presidential analytical requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early coordination can reduce later delays and disagreements over review scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and streamline internal rule development systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should review existing systems for developing and reviewing regulations to find bottlenecks, improve and streamline processes, and achieve more rapid internal clearances of proposed and final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use publicly announced schedules where feasible and develop reasoned analyses and responses to significant public comments to minimize review problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage the rulemaking file for maximum disclosure and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should manage rulemaking files so maximum disclosure is achieved during the comment period and a usable, reliable file is available for judicial review. The file should include notices, comments, and materials substantially relied upon or seriously considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials substantially relied on need not include every document in an agency’s files but should include those that significantly impacted agency thinking. Computerized access government-wide is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use negotiated/advisory committees and direct final rulemaking where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should use advisory or negotiated rulemaking committees where appropriate to improve quality and acceptability of rules and consider 'direct final' rulemaking for noncontroversial rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct final rulemaking: issue rule for notice and comment with statement that absent adverse comments the rule will become effective after a specified period (e.g., 30 days). Policies on advisory committees should be consistent with negotiated rulemaking use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider innovative public input methods and expedite noncontroversial rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider innovative methods for developing rules and obtaining public input and explore ways to reduce time required to develop final rules without eliminating opportunity for consideration and comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include negotiated rulemaking, direct final procedures, and other experimentation with oral or alternative procedures for particular contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure timely action on proposed rules and reconsider existing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should take steps to ensure proposed rules are acted on in a reasonably timely manner or withdrawn, and should evaluate and reconsider existing rules, initiating amendments and repeals where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency self-imposed deadlines are encouraged; agencies should periodically reassess existing regulations for relevance and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt proposed policies pending Congressional action when permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent permitted by law, agencies should adopt the proposed policies (e.g., management initiatives and procedural practices) pending Congressional action to amend the APA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encourages agencies to implement recommended best practices even before statutory changes take effect.
